page.layout: One text column of running prose, with marginal notes in the right margin beside the lines "vici tenent," and "munumen-" (the notes are small, in two-line groups). Running head at top, page number at top right. Signature "B 3" and catchword "cta," at the foot.

main_text.p: torium imperium, & jurisdictionem penè omnem soli Ripperdæi & Houverdæi, aut qui his succesfere, dudum nunc tenent, & quem volunt, Consulem, id est Redgerum, oppidanis dant. Iudices illorum vix umbram rei, cuius nomen ferunt, retinent, nec vocare quenquam, nec prehendere, nec coërcere, aut in vincula dare, non causas, non crimina cognoscere, nec de his, nec de illis sententias ferre possunt. De Dammona plus satis.

Reliqua per omnem agrum vici tenent,Vicinarum ea-rum numme-rus & cul-tus. & in his fanis insignes plus minus CLX[?]; quorum non pauci eâ magnitudine & cultu, ut oppidula videri queant. Cujusmodi sunt Visvleta ad Lavicam, & Nort-horma in Longowoldiis: Winsumum ad Hunesi flexum uno infra Groningam milliari: Bedumum, Vthusa, Middelst-hemum, Warfumum in Hunesgoniis: Lop-pershemum[?], Berumum, Farmsumum, & quæ nominata jam est Farmsumo proxima, unâque cum eo in orâ Amasi posita ad Fivelæ exitum, Delfsyla, amplis nunc munitionibus & firmis, velut urbs, cin-

page.notes: Library stamp at lower right omitted. The first word "torium" is a fragment from the previous page and is kept as such. "CLX" is read from a small, uneven numeral and marked [?]. "Lop-pershemum" and the marginal note's opening word are uncertain. The marginal note is transcribed as far as the scan allows; its first line is partly obscured by the print.
